and word, and uses a 16-byte local frame; retail saves type before the session
load, holds protocol in BL, stores the converted word in the dead data argument
slot and has a 12-byte frame.  The exact TCPConnection::Key_Exchange uses
separate load and conversion assignments; applying that pattern to all five
fields solved ACK1.  Test ACK2's session, port, and word separately and all
three together.  Each change preserves the original field's read, conversion,
type, and sequence.  Keep the ignored conversion untouched: introducing a named
value for it has historical coverage and would create a new local.

Each input is to be generated from the coordinator's explicit fresh source,

# Batch 2: remaining field load and session comparison

All three splits reduce the frame to the retail 12 bytes and match the entire
read section except the ignored 16-bit field: ours loads it into CX before
saving the previous conversion result; retail saves the previous result and
loads it into AX.  Represent that actual conversion with an assigned local,
using the same load/convert idiom, and independently reverse only the operands
of `c->Session != session`.  The latter addresses the retail `mov ecx,[c+8];
mov eax,ebp; ... cmp ecx,eax`, ours has these registers reversed; both operands
are plain integer reads and have no side effects.  Test both individually and
combined on the all-split input, preserving read and call order.  An ignored
conversion local was tried historically on a different unsplit source; this
combination is justified by the newly demonstrated frame and register change.

# Batch 3: real connection pointer scope

The all-split plus ignored-local form matches masked instructions and byte
length, but the actual retail uses the old len argument slot for the temporary
allocation and deleted handshake pointer and the old from slot for the new
connection; ours uses the opposite slots.  Test the real `con` pointer declared
before the loop, before `c`, and in a nested block ending after both list adds.
No constructor, add, delete, read or failure path is moved; pointers have
trivial destruction.  The goal is to change allocation of the two real locals,
not create padding or dead state.
